images.filename: Santa Rosa and San Jacinto Mountains 283.jpg
images.caption:
The North face of San Jacinto Mountains, the northernmost of the Peninsular Ranges, in Riverside County, Southern California.
From right to left the named summits in this picture are: Folly Peak, 10,480+ feet, San Jacinto Peak, 10,804 feet, Miller Peak, 10,400+ feet, and Cornell Peak, 9750 feet.
Protected within the Santa Rosa and San Jacinto Mountains National Monument, and the San Bernardino National Forest.
The steep escarpment of its north face climbs over 10,000 feet (3 km) in 7 miles (11.3 km). It is the steepest escaprtment in North America. Snow Creek can be seen as the snow-filled gully reaching to the summit. The lower reaches of Snow Creek belong to the Palm Springs Water District, which strictly enforces a ban on trespassing.

images.filename: -conservationlands15 Social Media Takeover, August 15th, Santa Rosa and San Jacinto National Monument in California (20402146310).jpg
images.caption:
Welcome to the August #conservationlands15 Social Media Takeover! Today’s 15th posts feature urban escapes - BLM National Conservation Lands close enough to home for everyday getaways, like the Santa Rosa and San Jacinto National Monument in California!
Rising abruptly from the desert floor near sea level, the Santa Rosa and San Jacinto Mountains National Monument reaches an elevation of 10,834 feet on Mount San Jacinto. The monument provides a picturesque backdrop to local desert communities including Palm Springs. Visitors can enjoy magnificent palm oases, snow-capped mountains, a national scenic trail, and wilderness areas. The area’s extensive trail network can be accessed from both the Coachella Valley and the alpine village of Idyllwild. Hikers can choose from over 20 trails, with some trailheads accessible right from town. The area has always been a city escape from Los Angeles, less than 2 hours to the west. The Palms to Pines Scenic Byway climbs from the valley floor to some of the highest reaches of the monument with numerous scenic viewpoints along the way. Don’t forget to use the new recreational map to find your way around the area.

Photo by Bob Wick
